market_context: United States/general English; raw or cooked meat outside refrigeration
title: How long can meat sit out?

seo.title: How long can meat sit out of the refrigerator?
seo.meta_description: Raw or cooked meat should not sit out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 °F. Grocery transport, prep, serving and counter time all count.
seo.search_intent: Know how long raw or cooked meat can remain unrefrigerated and when it should be discarded.

excerpt: USDA applies a 2-hour limit to perishable foods such as raw and cooked meat, reduced to 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 90 °F (32 °C). Exposure is cumulative: transport, preparation, serving and counter time all use the same safety margin.
content_html:
Meat does not have to smell bad to have spent too long warm. USDA's conservative limit is 2 hours outside refrigeration, or 1 hour when the temperature is above 90 °F (32 °C).

The rule covers raw and cooked meat

Raw steaks, ground meat, cooked roasts and leftovers are all perishable. Between roughly 40 and 140 °F, bacteria can multiply rapidly.

Time is cumulative

Thirty minutes driving home, 45 minutes during prep and an hour on the table total 2 hours 15 minutes. Refrigerating the food again does not erase earlier exposure.

Hot conditions cut the limit in half

Above 90 °F/32 °C, USDA reduces the limit to one hour. A sunny car or outdoor buffet can become much hotter than an indoor kitchen.

Cooking later does not rescue excessive exposure

Cooking kills many bacteria, but some organisms can produce heat-stable toxins. Meat that has clearly exceeded the recommended time should be discarded rather than “fixed” by extra cooking.

Smell and color cannot measure bacterial growth

Food can look and smell normal even after unsafe temperature exposure. Time and temperature history are more useful than a sensory check.

Long meals are where the rule is easiest to lose track of

At home we tend to count only counter time, but outdoor meals, barbecues and buffets can add exposure without anyone noticing the total. Serving smaller amounts and replenishing from the refrigerator or a properly hot holding dish reduces the time each portion spends in the danger zone.

The same logic applies to leftovers taken home: chilling them promptly matters more than waiting for them to “reach room temperature.” The goal is to minimize total warm time, not to cool food slowly.

Count all unrefrigerated time: 2 hours normally, 1 hour above 90 °F. Keep meat cold until you are ready to cook or serve it.

faq.question: Can I cook meat that sat out for 3 hours?
faq.answer: Three hours exceeds USDA's general 2-hour limit, so discarding it is the safer choice.

faq.question: Does cooked meat have the same rule?
faq.answer: Yes. Cooked meat and leftovers also need refrigeration within 2 hours, or 1 hour in hot conditions.

faq.question: Does putting it back in the fridge reset the clock?
faq.answer: No. Time outside refrigeration is cumulative.
